title: Automated Canary Analysis with Cross-Region Fallbacks and Tiered-Capacity Preemption
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement an Automated Canary Analysis (ACA) pipeline that evaluates model variants during canary and A/B rollouts, supports shadow traffic experiments, and coordinates routing fallback decisions across regions and capacity tiers. The system must detect semantic regressions and performance regressions automatically, apply policy-driven fallback (regional failover and tiered-capacity preemption), and trigger safe auto-rollbacks when thresholds are breached. This work includes a contract validator for model-variant compatibility (tokenizer, max context, kv-cache compatibility), integration points with the routing layer to support weighted traffic splits and immediate fallback when a variant becomes incompatible or unhealthy, and console/observability surfaces for per-canary diff views and historical comparisons.
acceptance_criteria: ACA engine computes a semantic-quality delta and performance delta for each canary run and publishes results to the canary dashboard
Auto-rollback executes when any of: semantic-quality drop > 2% absolute on canonical prompt set, P95 latency increase > 50ms (relative) for the route, or error rate > 0.5% for 5 continuous minutes

Routing layer supports cross-region hot-standby: if a primary region's canary fails, traffic moves to nearest healthy region without user-facing 5xxs and with a fallback variant described in the policy

Tiered-capacity preemption allows Dedicated pools to be preferred; when capacity is constrained, lower-priority shared pools can be preempted for critical traffic while maintaining SLA for reserved customers
Contract validator blocks canaries with incompatible tokenizer/config differences and reports specific incompatibilities in the UI
Shadow traffic mode can run at scale for up to 24h with no production-side effect and produces paired metrics for comparison
Per-canary diff view in Console shows side-by-side examples, aggregated metrics, and a signal-quality score; historical canary runs are retained for 90 days
End-to-end test harness with synthetic traffic exercises routing failovers and auto-rollback triggers in CI
implementation_steps: Define canonical prompt/eval set for semantic quality (initial seed from research/evals team)
Build ACA service: ingest canary samples, compute semantic similarity (embedding-based + lexical checks), compute traffic-weighted performance metrics, and produce a verdict and reason codes
Add model-variant contract validator: tokenizer sanity checks, max-context, kv-cache shape compatibility, and quantization flag checks
Extend routing service to accept ACA verdicts and execute fallback actions (region switch, variant substitution, capacity preemption)
Expose hooks in Console for starting canaries, viewing live ACA results, and manual override/rollback
Instrument dashboards and alerts (PagerDuty thresholds) for high-severity auto-rollback events
Write end-to-end tests and chaos tests that simulate OOMs, tokenization mismatches, and cross-region latency spikes
testing_plan: Unit tests for ACA signal calculations and contract validator
Integration tests: simulated canary runs with synthetic prompts comparing baseline vs canary (shadow and canary modes)
Canary smoke: run 1% canary with controlled perturbations to validate metric sensitivity
Chaos testing in staging: force region-level failures and verify routing fallback and no user-visible 5xxs
Post-rollout GA experiment: A/B cohort checks to validate no long-tail regressions over 7 days
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal staging rollout with shadow traffic for 72h and gated ACA acceptance. Phase 2: 0.5% public canary for 24h with full ACA + manual review. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 10% over 48h with automatic rollback enabled. Final: enable cross-region hot-standby and tiered preemption for limited set of routes during the following release window.
